$comment: Executable data contract. Every example here is run against the real parser by backend/test/data-contract.test.js, and docs/CONTRATO-DATOS.md is generated from it. If the parser and this file ever disagree, the test fails rather than the documentation lying.

accepted.name: units
accepted.why: the measured value; the whole point of the file

accepted.name: unidades
accepted.why: the Spanish header, which is what a Colombian export usually carries

accepted.name: qty
accepted.why: what most POS systems name it

accepted.name: ventas
accepted.why: some systems export the sold count under this name

accepted.name: value
accepted.why: generic, but unambiguous in a two-column file

accepted.name: demanda
accepted.why: what the model is predicting, named as such

notAccepted.name: precio
notAccepted.why: a price is not a demand count, so accepting it would model money instead of units

notAccepted.name: total
notAccepted.why: ambiguous between a line total and a day total

notAccepted.name: stock
notAccepted.why: not a demand measure. See openColumns below.

notAccepted.name: inventario
notAccepted.why: same: a quantity on hand, not a quantity sold

accepted.name: dia
accepted.why: Spanish for day, with or without the accent

accepted.name: periodo
accepted.why: some BI exports label the column this way

formats.why: unambiguous, and the safest thing to send
what Colombian Excel writes. Read as DAY first.

dayFirstIsMandatory.rule: Any slash, hyphen or dot date is read DAY first. There is no way to detect which convention the writer used from the shape alone.

danger.butMayMean: 4 March, if the file came from a month-first system
danger.consequence: the series is silently out of order and the weekly seasonality the model depends on becomes noise. The model still returns a WAPE, so nothing looks wrong.
danger.mitigation: Re-export as YYYY-MM-DD and that question disappears. If you cannot, tell us your convention and we will read the file accordingly.
danger.detection: If the dates go backwards, the evaluation returns a high-severity finding naming the offending lines. That catches the mistake after the fact; it cannot undo it.

delimiters.why: the safe default: what a POS export and a developer both produce
Spanish-locale Excel. Detected from the first line, so it does not need to be declared anywhere.
tab-separated, which is what some BI tools emit

lexicalTolerances.why: optional. A file of nothing but numbers is a valid series.
any line starting with # is ignored, which is where the note to the reader goes
quotes are stripped, and a doubled quote inside is an escaped quote
tolerated, because a Windows copy/paste adds one and it would otherwise hide the header
the dot groups thousands and the comma is the decimal, in that locale

refusals.why: a negative sale is a return, which needs the returns included, not netted into a demand series
below 28 days there is not enough left after a 14-day holdout to fit a weekly season
above 365 days. Not a limit of interest, a guard against a stray multi-year file.
there is no way to tell which column is the demand measure

refusals.case: comma decimal in a comma-delimited file
refusals.why: 1,234 is either 1234 or 1.234 and guessing wrong is a 1000x error in the data, so it is refused instead
2026-02-31 is not rolled forward into March; the date is dropped and gap detection is lost for that row
the body carried neither an array nor csv text

openColumns.name: stock_disponible
openColumns.why: This is the most valuable thing a retailer could send and the parser will refuse it as a third column. A zero on a day the shelf was empty is not zero demand, and the diagnostics can only report that it happened, not act on it. Excluding those days before fitting would make the WAPE honest rather than merely flagged.
openColumns.nextStep: A stock flag turns the diagnostics from a warning into a correction. Say so when you send the request: it is the difference between a demo and a pilot.

openColumns.name: precio / promocion
openColumns.why: Price explains a demand spike, so it belongs in the model eventually. It is not needed for the first evaluation and would make the first conversation harder.

openColumns.name: sku / producto
openColumns.why: The endpoint takes a single series. To compare products, send one file per SKU. Multi-series is what the phase-two dashboard adds.

whatTheCustomerGetsBack: WAPE of the model against a seasonal-naive baseline, on the same held-out days
the improvement in error, and the money that is worth at their own contribution margin
a data-quality report: stock-out runs named by date, calendar gaps, promotion-sized outliers
a stored record with a 90-day retention, readable back through the same API
